utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Mr. Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar. No preliminaries were announced. Therefore, is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It is, Mr. President. The next witness is Ian Hanson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the -- there seems to be a problem with the audio for Mr. Mladic. Could we first sort that out. Mr. Mladic, can you now hear me in a language you understand? Apparently not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Does it work now, Mr. Mladic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can you now hear me in a language -- yes, I see that Mr. Mladic confirms that he receives audio in his own language. Then could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And as the witness is entering, perhaps we could meanwhile call up 65 ter 31099.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration, of which the text is now handed out to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated, Mr. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, you'll first be examined by Mr. Tieger. You find Mr. Tieger to your right. Mr. Tieger is counsel for the Prosecution. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Although we are well aware by now, if you could state your name for the record, please.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Ian David Hanson.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you are the deputy director of forensic science of the ICMP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, please pause between question and answer and the other way around.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that is an excellent reminder from His Honour, and I'm the offender here but we should both pause because we speaking the same language and we need to leave time for the interpretation. Can you briefly describe for Their Honours the nature of your work as deputy director of forensic science.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. Within the ICMP I manage the archaeology and anthropology division. This undertakes assistance to governments and authorities in the search, excavation, and examination of missing persons.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And does that entail assistance with authorities in locating and excavating grave-sites, mass graves, and so on?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, I've called up 65 ter 31099. This is your curriculum vitae; is that correct? You will see that on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now I appreciate that to a large extent that it speaks for itself, but if could identify just a few highlights and ask you to confirm them. First of all, you've had 26 years of archaeological experience; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that would include approximately 16.000 hours of field investigations including many which you have supervised and directed around the world including in the Balkans, the Middle East, and Africa?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You are senior lecturer or have been a senior lecturer in forensic archaeology at Bournemouth University?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: You have designed and managed training courses in this field?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And you have published and lectured extensively as reflected in the CV including a book in 2008 entitled: "The Scientific Investigation of Mass Graves Towards Protocols and Standard Operating Procedures"?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd tender 65 ter 31099.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7430, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, in your capacity as deputy director, were you called upon to assist in the exhumation at the Tomasica site in 2013?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, I was. We were contacted by the prosecutor's office to assist, I think, on 6th of September 2013.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Had you been contacted in connection with the possibility of an excavation of Tomasica prior to the time it began?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, I was. We met with the missing persons institute in, I recall, December 2012 where they discussed with us whether a return to that particular site was warranted given previous findings and the current information they had, and in 2013 those discussions continued as to the potential to go to that site to undertake further investigations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, I noticed that you are now and then are looking at papers which are before you. The Chamber is not aware of what they are, and usually we ask witnesses not to do that, and if they need to do it to tell us, and then also to tell us what you're looking at.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Fine, Your Honour. I was just referring to my report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Fine. That's -- it's your report which you have before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Nothing else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I should have intervened before the Presiding Judge was required to do so. I will be referring you during the course of the examination to portions of your report, some of which will be shown on screen, others in the interest of time we may just ask you to look to yourself and confirm. So clearly I would have asked you to refer to a hard copy document in front of you and should have addressed that, but it's good we have that on the record now. You've just indicated the discussions that resulted in conclusions that could be worthwhile to further explore the Tomasica site. Was trenching probes subsequently undertaken after that discussion?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, I was contacted by the prosecutor's office on 6th of September, 2013, to be informed that they had undertaken probing, test trenching at the Tomasica location on the 4th of -- and 5th of September, 2013.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And although it may be implicit in what you've just said, did that initial trenching on the 4th and 5th of September reveal the presence of remains, human remains at the site?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the telephone call from the prosecutor's office stated that they had found human remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you describe for Their Honours the nature of your role or assistance thereafter.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, I was asked by the prosecutor's office to assist in advising on the technical aspect of the excavation - that is, the archaeological works, the logistics works of excavating - and that's one of the primary roles ICMP undertakes in assisting the prosecutor's office and other authorities in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 42 of your report indicates that the excavation process was overseen by the deputy director of forensic sciences, yourself, supported by ICMP archaeologists. In a general manner, does that accurately describe your role in connection with the excavation?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, overseeing the excavation. And in that providing advise to the prosecutor and missing persons institute and other staff on the site as how to proceed with those technical matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 43 goes on to describe the technical advice in a general manner that was rendered via recommendations based on ICMP guide-lines, procedures, archaeological best practice, and so on. Does that fairly characterise the nature of ICMP's efforts and your own efforts regarding the excavation at the site; that is, to ensure that the best practices, proper procedures and protocols and methods were adhered to?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 43 also goes on to discuss or describe stratigraphic excavation, the delineation and recording of soil stratigraphy to determine a full deposition in chronological sequence, and so on. Is that a description of the kind of information that can be revealed through the adherence to the protocols and procedures you discussed; that is, the unfolding of an archaeological record of what happened?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's the -- the standard result that can be achieved from excavation using archaeological principles.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you indicate to the Court with whom you worked? You've already indicated that you were present at the request of the BiH prosecutor's office. During the course of your efforts to oversee the excavation, what other officials were involved in that process?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The missing persons institute were constantly present at the excavation. The excavation was secured by the Prijedor police, and they also provided crime technicians who did the evidence numbering, recording, and gathering into chain of custody. At times, the court-appointed medical expert was also present; workers from the mortuary company from Sanski Most were present to assist the excavation; and latterly, the Tuzla Commemorative Centre provided a small excavating machine and driver to assist with the excavation; and ICMP staff were present as required to assist with the technical support of the work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that can be found, I believe, at pages 4 and 5 of your report; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, 4 and 5 lists the participants present during the excavation. At some dates the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia also had a senior investigator present. And just to note at the -- on page 5 survey and archaeological data collection analysis and planning, that was -- work was undertaken after the excavation and involved three persons who were doing the post-excavation analysis to produce plans and maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hanson, did you prepare a report about the Tomasica excavation that detailed the chronology process, procedures, and findings in connection with that work?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we call up 65 ter 31086, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This is an 83-page document, the cover of which you now see in front of you. I can -- and we will be going through portions of that. If you need to see more to identify it, I'm happy to show you. But is that sufficient to -- for you to know whether or not that is the report that you prepared?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that is my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in addition to the report itself, and the substance of which we will be discussing during the course of this morning, is it correct that the document also contains a number of appendices at the end of it?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And do those include the following: A glossary of the terms used in the report that may not be immediately apparent to the lay reader?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: A list of acronyms?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: An explanation of archaeological symbols that are used?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: A list of the archaeological context found during the excavation?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Section drawings revealing the stratigraphy; that is, the order and relative position of a strata?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Plans showing the distribution of the remains?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Location maps?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: List of human remains found and their locations?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And references?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Kindly pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I raise those at the outset as a reminder that we have those resources as we're going through the examination either for reference by the Bench or any of the parties now or subsequently. Your Honours, consistent with case practice, I would not tender this document for admission at this time but ask that it be marked for identification pending completion of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, what number would be assigned to document to be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be MFI P7431, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, I'd like to discuss some aspects of the report as I indicated previously. So setting aside the executive summary at the beginning of the report, the report begins at paragraph 25 on page 9 with what appears to be a short section on the background to the excavation which is followed by information on the location and geology of the site beginning at paragraphs 34; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you a little initially about the general area of the site. Turning to page 70 of your report, do figures 55 and 56 indicate generally where Prijedor is and provide some Google Earth imagery of the area?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: They do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also MGRS - that is, military grid reference system co-ordinates - in your report and is that contained on page 4?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, if you would allow me just a short observation. Yesterday we looked at aerial images of the area as well. I now see that on page 70 that we -- this is apparently oriented north which makes me conclude that what we saw yesterday with another witness was not the usual south/north orientation. Could the Prosecution in order to avoid that we always have to turn our necks in such a direction try to always present materials in a similar way; that is north up, south down, and not like yesterday where it was difficult. It is difficult for us to compare the different images if they're all differently oriented.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Understood, Mr. President. We'll bear that request in mind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you to focus a little more closely on the specific area of the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in that respect, I'd call up 65 ter 31077. Okay. And I'd ask that the -- this is a general plan of the Ljubija iron-ore mine. Perhaps we could try to blow it up a little bit more for the benefit of the witness and the parties and the Bench. I think it's going to be still hard to read. Perhaps we could dispense with the key for the moment and just have it full screen and then blow it up. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Are you able to recognise with that degree of magnification, Mr. Hanson, the area depicted?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, I am. I can see Prijedor and the area of the Tomasica mine, which is central to this image.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And we see Prijedor at the upper left quadrant of the map the road leading downward, and can you show us with the pen that will be provided by the usher where the Tomasica mine site is located.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Thank you. It's the area I've circled.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can I tender 65 ter 31077, Mr. President. I should also note that it is page 3 in the Tomasica map book which has previously been marked as P7417.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit P7432, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And for the record, this is the marked version; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, had this site been excavated or probed before 2013 and is that discussed in paragraph 26 of your report?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. We determined there were previous excavations, and the nature of that work was described in existing reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When was the first one?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: There had been a probe of the site in 2002 under the auspices of ICTY.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And was that successful in finding remains; and, if not, why not, to the extent it was known?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The report states that no mass graves were found, although extensive trenching was undertaken. It appears from examining that report the trenches were not deep enough to reach the grave or the relative features of any remains that were later revealed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were further excavations undertaken in 2004; and if so, with what result?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: They were. Paragraph 27 describes this. A grave was found during further excavations in 2004. 117 cases were recovered which represented a minimum of 23 individuals. That work was stopped due to rainstorms and flooding. There was a resumption later in 2004, and the site was returned to in 2006 for further excavations of the same grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you explain the difference between cases and minimum number of individuals, please.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: A case describes a designation of evidence, and this may be a body, or part of a body, it may be an artefact, or anything else that the authorities at the excavation define as useful and wish to seize into evidence. The MNI, minimum number of individuals, this is a calculation made by the anthropological assessment of remains to determine how many individuals may be present by counting the bones. Where there are repeats of the same bone, such as a cranium, it indicates there must be more than one individual. However, this technique only gives a minimum number.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to the nature of the remains found there and the assessment of minimum number of individuals, was any determination made at that time about whether or not they represented all of the human remains that had initially been placed at that site?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: From the report, it simply describes the number of cases recovered and the -- and a brief summary of the excavation. However, it was known that the site linked to a secondary grave location called Jakarina Kosa, which had been excavated in 2001, which I state in paragraph 30. We know from subsequent DNA analysis that cases - that is, human remains from the same individual - were found in both locations.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And during the 2004 excavations, were only -- I think we can see that from the distinction between cases and individuals, but I'll ask you that: Were only complete bodies found or were body parts, isolated body parts found, and in general was there an assessment made about whether or not the grave-site had been left intact or had been disturbed?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: No, the report states that bodies and body parts were recovered, and it states that the site had been robbed of most of the remains after initial burial with many isolated body parts found during the 2004 exhumation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And that is linked to your previous observation about the secondary site at Jakarina Kosa and the linkage between the two?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that was reported upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And I may ask you that later, but if you could very briefly indicate what is meant by "secondary site"?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Secondary site or secondary grave describes a location to which remains have been taken from a location of initial and primary intern.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there further excavation at the same location in 2006?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And with what results?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Of the two bodies and eight body parts were recovered from re-excavation of the 2004 site works.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're now talking -- again, not about Jakarina Kosa but now we're back in Tomasica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we always if we're talking about a location to be very clear which one is referred to. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And was it again assessed that the grave-site had been robbed with removal of the contents?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could quickly turn back to P74 -- excuse me. 7432. Still there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could you indicate, if you can see it on the map, where the Jakarina Kosa site is located?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the Jakarina Kosa site is located west of the Tomasica site. I cannot tell from the map the exact location, but this is within this general area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And for benefit of the Judges there's a key, which we could revert back to if we resumed the split-screen, that indicates Jakarina Kosa by a number that is reflected in the map itself, and I believe that's number 19 in the key. If we could go to the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In the original it's exactly the same, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Right. Then perhaps we could go back quickly to 65 ter 31077. Before we move, let's have this marked as well since it was marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, the second marking now ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, in order not to scatter all the information, I suggest that first we have a technical problem that it may -- we may need to have the Jakarina Kosa to be re-marked. But if we do it in a different colour and then all in the same document so that red marking is Tomasica and then the blue marking is Jakarina Kosa. Could the usher assist the witness in marking again after the ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: While we do that, Mr. Tieger, just to remind you -- you said could we go back quickly to 65 ter 31077, just to remind you that 31077 is this P7432.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The unmarked version.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And we also have the -- the document in the map book as well, so I appreciate that reminder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I suggest that we admit in evidence under the same number this map now marked in red for Tomasica and in blue for Jakarina Kosa. Mr. Registrar -- and that would then be number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P7432.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so the new version now with the second marking on it replaces the original one. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, you mentioned earlier Jakarina Kosa as a secondary site and the fact that it was excavated. That's referred to in paragraph 30 of your report; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell us what the results of that 2001 excavation were?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It was published that 139 bodies, 259 body parts were recovered from the site, with a minimum number of individuals calculated 298 based on anthropology.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. So that 139 intact bodies, 259 body parts, and based on the anthropological assessment a total of 298 -- minimum number of 298 distinct individuals?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you get any indication of how difficult or complex an investigation -- an excavation this was?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, I did. The site is an open-cast mine. That's the type of mine that has many steps and is used for the extractions of ores and minerals that forms a very deep pit or excavation into the landscape, and it was on the slope and side of this mine that the excavation took place, so it was complicated and quite difficult and dangerous work.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And do you know how the remains that you referred to a moment ago - that is, the minimum number of 298 - how they were covered up when the site was excavated?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It was reported to me by the MPI in the prosecutor's office that they had information that an explosion blasted the rock and soil at the site from the side of the mine to cover the remains.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I ask that we go into private session very quickly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So, Mr. Hanson, is it correct, therefore, that it is thought by persons familiar with that 2001 excavation and the site itself that not all of the remains at that site have been recovered?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Hanson, the next section of the report appears to be entitled: "Method," that's section 5, which begins at paragraph 42, which is on page 13. And does that cover the following: The archaeological excavation of the grave and other features?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The archaeological excavation of the remains and other evidence?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the documentation and recovery of the remains and evidence?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So I'd like to ask you a few questions about some of those aspects of the excavation. Now, in paragraph 44 at page 13, you refer to the initial trenching and discovery of multiple complete bodies lying in a deposit of mixed yellow-grey clay over which was a mixture of brown clay. If we could turn to page 14, specifically Figure 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And perhaps we could call that up in MFI 7431. And if we could magnify the top half, please, specifically Figure 3. And although I appreciate that Mr. Lukic can follow, that is B/C/S page 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does that depict the nature of the clay that you referred to in the earlier paragraph, in paragraph 44?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The excavation you can see in the foreground is the initial trenching undertaking on the 4th and 5th of September 2013 by the prosecutor's office and MPI. You can see the difference there in the section, that's the vertical view, you can see the lighter yellow-grey clay, and distinct from that the mixed brown clay. Above the trench, you can see the machine excavating. It's undertaken on the work on the -- after the 4th and 5th September to ascertain the extent of the -- these deposits.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the multiple complete bodies referred to in paragraph 44 were found within the yellow-grey clay; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And the mixed brown clay covered that yellow grey-clay up and much of the site; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now you also detail in the method section, which goes from pages 13 to 23, the general process that followed the identification of the remains within that yellow-grey clay, but perhaps we can begin by discussing briefly what happened after the -- happened in the process after the initial indication of remains reflected in paragraph 44. So, first, just focusing on that portion of your report that deals with the excavation of the grave, was there an effort made to determine the extent of the mixed brown clay that was covering up the yellow clay in which the bodies and body parts were found?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes there was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that reflected in paragraph 45 of your report?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just briefly, what was done?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: As we can see in Figure 3, the mixed brown clay overlay the yellow-grey clay, and we needed to determine the extent of the mixed brown clay; if this was a deposit covering the graves, we needed to find out how extensive it was. And two trenches and one sondage, which is a wider trench, were dug in different directions from the initial trenching, the initial excavation, to determine the extent of the mixed brown clay, and that's illustrated in Figure 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could scroll down the page slightly, you will see Figure 4 in its entirety. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And after the determination of the extent of the mixed brown clay, was it -- did a stripping process then begin to get down to the mixed yellow clay and the remains?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it was discussed and agreed that the mixed brown clay should be removed to reveal the yellow-grey clay and anything else lying beneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 51 of your report indicates that the clay was removed from within the feature in spits. What does that refer to?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Removal in spits is the removal of material in uniform layers so the removal can be controlled and observed so that any pertinent evidence can be gathered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, could I ask an explanation from the witness. On Figure 4, we see the first trench and the second trench and the sondage depicted there. Now in the sondage, there seems to be a cut more or less. Could you explain what that is? You see that it's -- if up would be north, it goes from south-west to north-east, it's a brown line in the middle of the wide area, which is determined as sondage. You see what I mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Figure 4, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, in Figure 4. Close to the centre.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You see -- if -- if the usher could assist with the -- with the cursor. Yes, it's exactly there. You see that there's a brown line crossing the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you explain what that is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's simply a gap between the edge of the initial trenching and the start of the sondage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the sondage -- yes. And that's perhaps only 1 or 2 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it's about a metre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And what's the reason why you split them up? Why don't you just go on for the 2 metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In practical terms, the -- a gap was left to retain the section of the initial trench so that we could record the soil deposits without first destroying them. We wanted to leave them so they could be protected so they could be thoroughly recorded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: At paragraph 55 of your report, you then indicate the initiation of identification pin-pointing of the remains after a month of excavation and the -- in paragraph 56, the systematic recording and recovery of the bodies and other remains and evidence. I just wanted to ask you if all of the mixed brown clay was stripped before the identification of remains began and the recovery of those remains or if that proceeded in a sequenced fashion?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the mixed brown clay was removed from the area of the initial trenching to expose what was revealed to be an extensive feature, which was sub-rectangular in shape. Within that feature, excavation of further mixed brown soil revealed remains. While the examination of this feature, which was determined to be a grave, continued, the heavy machinery around the grave continued to strip the mixed brown clay as we realised this was an extensive operation and these activities needed to be undertaken simultaneously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, I'm sorry to interrupt, but I -- in order not to print out everything, I have the PDF file of the originally submitted report, and there's a bit of a problem because Figure 10 in that original version is followed by paragraph number 43, and then it continues again with 56 on the next page after Figure 11. So apparently there are two versions, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I apologise for the fact that the Bench apparently -- is apparently the only people in the room not aware of that. We discovered that too. The document that had been previously in e-court was replaced with a properly formatted version which had been provided by ICMP and Mr. Hanson. We notified the Defence about that before it was done. Fortunately, Mr. Lukic had been working off the B/C/S version which was correctly formatted, so it caused him no difficulties. I apologise for not ensuring that the Bench was aware of that. But the version currently in e-court has the correct formatting which has the paragraphs numbered in proper sequence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, we have no access to those e-court new versions while preparing for the examination of the witness, so therefore I worked on the old one. And in order to avoid that, we have to print out. But it's clear now that I have to -- whenever you now refer to a paragraph number that I have to adapt to the new paragraph numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's partly why I had been also referring to page numbers in virtually all circumstances. But possibly with a small exception, if there's a bleed-over sentence, the page numbers are still the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That has been clarified. Thank you very much. Please proceed -- oh no, please don't proceed because we'll take a break first. Mr. Hanson, we'll take a break of 20 minutes. We'd like to see you back after the break and you may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, as far as time is concerned, are we on track.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah. Numerically, we are precisely on track. Nevertheless, I'm going to look through my materials to see if I can ensure that there's no risk of slipping over. It's my intention to adhere closely to the time-limit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's appreciated. We take a break and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber was informed that there was a scheduling issue to be raised.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. That's correct. And if I could ask that we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. President, may I also indicate that we are in process of printing out three copies of the correct version which are -- which will arrive imminently and which we will --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, we will try to stop you there, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Oh.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Why? Because yesterday I instructed my personal assistant not to print out the version, which I can easily consult on my screen. One copy will do. In order to save paper, and -- because I have the new version now electronically available and can work on that as well. If it's done already, then don't forget it for the next time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I was just looking at the new version but please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, at page 26 of your report, we see a section entitled: "Results." Let me ask you a few quick questions about the findings and results.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: First of all, how long was the excavation?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The excavation took 79 working days.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did it reveal the presence of graves; and, if so, how many?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. Three separate graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 23, Figure 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 86, which is the first paragraph under the results section, you indicate a main grave, Trench 1, and a rectangular grave, as the graves where remains were found, and could you indicate to the Court if those are depicted in Figure 17.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, they are. The excavations of those graves are indicated in Figure 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And perhaps we could also turn to Figure 31 at page 37. All right. And does that more precisely or accurately depict the outlines of the main grave; and, if so, could you point out exactly where that is found?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that indicates the edge of the grave as recorded of the main grave. Would you like me to mark the figure?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Please. Or just point it out and we'll describe it -- okay.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's fine. And that's basically in the middle of Figure 31 immediately above the title: "Edge of Grave"; correct?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Correct, as I've marked it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There are titles "Edge of Grave," but it's the left one, I take it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The left one in the centre of the location.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The other one, I remember from the previous, was about the re-excavation of 2004. The one more to the right.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So it's the centre one with this title just above that text. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And is it correct that the configuration in Figure 17 of the main grave indicates the areas where stripping and excavation work was undertaken to identify the precise outlines of the main grave?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's it. The excavation trench was larger than the grave because areas needed to be excavated to assist with safe work access of machinery and control of water ingress into the grave during rain.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now we mentioned the annexes before. Is there an annex that contains all of the cases found and their location?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: There is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is that Annex 4 at page 72?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And does Annex 4 indicate not only the list of cases but also where they were found among the different deposits?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the main grave, can we look quickly at Figure 42 at page 47. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The marking is still on the screen covering now the new site.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'm not sure how we can eliminate that marking, but -- meanwhile, because I'm not going to introduce that or we're not going to mark this exhibit, this page -- fine. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Does Figure 42 indicate the different deposits - that is, the 12 deposits for the main grave - and label them?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could blow that up slightly. So those are marked 1, 1A, 1B, 1C, 2, 2A, and so on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: For a total of 12. Now those figures represented in Figure 42, what are those based on?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Those are based on the three-dimensional survey data recorded for the position of each body at the time of excavation which would were then rendered as stick figures using software so that it can be -- the position of each body in relation to the other can visually be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, you've already indicated that Annex 4 contains a listing of all the cases and the -- broken down as we saw from a quick glance at Annex 4 by complete bodies, body parts, and general bones. Does the report also provide numbers of complete bodies and body parts and general bones in the executive summary and conclusion?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And does it also provide a breakdown of the totals by grave-site in paragraph 86, on pages 26 and 27?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, do those numbers precisely conform or are there any differences between the totals listed in the executive summary and conclusion and in the -- in paragraph 86 from the annex?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: They don't conform. There where some typos.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Which document or which section of the report should the Court look to for the definitive understanding of how many cases were identified and their breakdown into complete bodies, body parts, and general bones?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: A complete list in Annex 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And can you explain briefly what accounts for the difference between the numbers in the executive summary and conclusion or the -- or paragraph 86 from the annex?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, there were some errors in tallying - that is, counting - which cases were in which deposit, and that was simply some errors in tallying from the original data from the paperwork from the field and the survey data.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, what kind of differences are we talking about? Large numbers or small numbers?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: No, very small numbers. The total number of cases recorded is correct, the total number of bodies recovered is the same. There is some difference between total number of body parts designated as D and the general bone cases designated as GB.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson earlier referred to the information that can be understood through the preservation of the archaeological record.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to preserve the archaeological record in the course of this excavation and on that basis were you able to discern the chronology of activity related to this grave-site?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, we were able to accurately record the archaeological record and undertake an analysis and interpretation from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that discussed at the section entitled: "Phases of the Archaeological Record" beginning at -- at paragraph 89 on page 27 of your report?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, at paragraph 89 it indicates "the chronology of events from latest to earliest are," so is it correct that there the chronology is listed essentially in reverse order; that is, from the most recent event to the earliest?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It is because that is the sequence in which the archaeological deposits are encountered during excavation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in your conclusion, is the sequence of events listed in the order in which they actually occurred?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the conclusion provides a chronological order to the archaeological phases identified and analysed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now that seems to begin at paragraph 132 on page 52, which begins: "Clear phases of activity were seen in the archaeological record ..." And I want to run through those quickly with you. First of all in paragraph 132, you state that all graves were dug through the same ground surface and --

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that the -- was that the yellow-grey clay that we saw in, I believe, Figure 3 or 4 that you referred to a while back?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. After removal of the mixed brown clay, it was revealed that upper surface of the yellow brown clay formed a common surface across the site through which all the graves had been dug.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So does that represent the landscape before -- at Tomasica before the bodies were first put in there?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you find any evidence of any mining or excavation activity in that part of the site that preceded the grave construction?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: No, we did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine how the graves were dug; that is, by what means or equipment?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The size of the graves, the width of trenches 1 and 2, and the finding of machine tool marks in the surface of the yellow-grey clay are consistent with the use of heavy machinery; that is, large excavators they used in construction and industry.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When you say the size of trenches 1 and 2, what are you referring to specifically?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The width of the trench is indicative of the width of the machine bucket used to excavate such a trench.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Paragraph 133 then goes on to note that a phase of filling the graves followed. And you mention the 12 deposits which we previously saw depicted in -- in the Figure 42. Does the -- does 12 deposits mean 12 separate periods of activity?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It may have done. But from the positioning of the deposits in the bodies, I can say with confidence there are a minimum of four periods of activity.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And how are you able to identify that from the archaeological record?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: By the numbering and sequence of deposits above the deposits at the bottom of the grave. It's possible that several of the body deposits could have been placed simultaneously; however, when one body deposit is on top of another body deposit, they could not have been placed simultaneously. So we can say a minimum of four, but there are also 12 separate deposits of bodies identified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That answer is still not perfectly clear how. You say it's possible that several of the body deposits could have been placed simultaneously. That I understand. However, when one body deposit is on top of another -- of course, you can't put them exactly at the same time but if bodies are in heaps, why -- where do you draw a line between what is one deposit and what's the next deposit which is not simultaneously made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The body deposits we could differentiate because they were separated by layers of clay --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this -- we don't know -- we cannot tell from the excavation how rapidly these were placed, but definitely we can see between deposits of body layers of clay which must have been placed over each deposit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's rather the separation than the one being above the other.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to determine -- to find indications of how much time may have transpired between the deposits of bodies that were separated by clay?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Exactly timings, no; however, in all the intact body deposits it was noticed that the bodies were very well preserved. There was little decomposition, and this is consistent with burial quite soon after death dependant upon climate, weather conditions, time of year.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that what you referred to in paragraph 83, page 24, of your report in connection with the compression of the bodies and the nature of the clay?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the depth and the nature of the clay has a preventative effect on decomposition. This has been observed in many excavations as a prevention of decay due to the environment within the grave. Oxygen, in effect, is prevented from entering the grave by the dense nature of the clay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger it seems to me that we're now following up on a matter which was not the core of your question. The question was, as far as I understood, how much time passed between one deposit and another one; whereas, your answer focused on how long after death the deposit was made. And that's -- these are two separate -- different things, if I understood your question well and if I understood the answer well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness can explain that. In what way does that factor relate to the issue of the time between the -- that the Court is quite correct. So focusing on the time between the deposits, which you answered, my question should have been more precisely: Do you have any indication of how long bodies were in the grave before they were covered by the clay material that separated them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, that's another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I agree. I think you identified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We have now three questions. The first one was how much time passed between the deposit of bodies and then the next series of bodies being deposited. The second question now is how long -- how much time passed between the deposit of the bodies and the covering layer of clay. And the third one, the third question, was -- well, perhaps not put but you addressed it, is how much time passed between death of the persons and the -- position in the grave. We have three questions now and --

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if I can assist the witness. I think he did answer what the third -- he provided information on the third one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The last one was answered -- yes, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I have replaced that first question with the second.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the only question is does the -- do the factors identified in paragraph 84 - that is, the compression of the bodies, the nature of the clay, and the relative preservation that you found - shed light on the time that may have elapsed between the placement of the bodies in the grave and their covering up with the clay.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. The preservation of the bodies would suggest that they were covered after a short time. There was no time for decomposition to take place before the bodies were covered with the layers of clay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: All right. In paragraph 133, you indicate that the bodies were covered with clay and the grave backfilled. Backfilling meaning what, Mr. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The covering of the grave with material.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And would that have been the same material that had been removed from the grave in order to place the bodies in?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the clay we found filling the top of the grave over the bodies is consistent with the material through which the grave had been dug; that is, the yellow-grey clay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that what you indicate in paragraph 103 at page 34?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Similarly at paragraph 107 on page 35, you talk about trench 1 filled with a deposit of mixed yellow-grey clay covering an intact and undisturbed deposit of bodies and conclude this is consistent with the material that was dug out to create the grave then being used to refill the grave. Are both of those factors part of the archaeological record that led to the conclusion about the backfilling of the graves following the deposit of the bodies?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Then at paragraph 135, page 53, you indicate that a phase consistent with the intentional disturbance and removal of remains then followed. Okay. And is that a way of talking about what you referred to in -- earlier in another context, the robbing of the grave?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. We recorded robbed areas of the grave where remains had been disturbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now in that same paragraph, you talked about a disturbance in the main grave and rectangular grave with bodies truncated and removed, body parts dispersed in and around the grave that had originated with the in situ deposits of bodies, trauma observed on remains, and damage to remains consistent with removal by heavy machinery, and evidence of heavy machinery found in the form of tool marks. I'd like to go through some of those factors with you one by one. First of all, the disturbance and truncation and removal, and in that connection can we turn to page 46 and look at Figure 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if that can be done on the screen as well, please. And if we could enlarge the bottom portion of the figure below Figure 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us, please, what that depicts.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, in this figure, we see the outline of the grave, the bodies and body parts as found are represented as stick figures as recorded through the detailed surveying. You have two areas marked with a dash line. In these areas, mixed brown clay was found and numerous body parts; that is, parts of bodies. These areas of mixed brown clay and body parts went up to and stopped at the edge of the intact piles of bodies which you can see numbered.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With respect to the presence of mixed brown clay, could we turn to page 33 and look quickly at Figure 26. Now, that indicates that the robbing cut indicated by arrows and the mixed brown clay filling it can be contrasted with the pre-existing mine waste deposits which the main grave cuts through. So is that an indication of one of the robbing cuts that you saw and that are shown to the archaeological record?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. When you refer to the pre-existing mine waste deposits, does that refer to the yellow grey clay into which the graves were initially dug and the bodies initially placed?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is it correct that we see on the right portion the yellow-grey clay running down to the bottom surface, and in the left portion the mixed brown clay filling that portion of the grave?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court how that would have occurred?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The filling of the grave with the mixed brown clay, for clarification?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: How -- how the existence of robbing cuts is -- is reflected in the presence of mixed brown clay where there had previously been a yellow-grey clay?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the space between the existing yellow-brown -- sorry, the yellow-grey clay within the grave and the deposits of bodies was filled with mixed brown clay, and the mixed brown clay did not extend beyond an edge formed of yellow-grey clay and bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me step back a bit and try to make the question a little bit more clear. The landscape at the outset, if I understood your testimony correctly, is yellow-grey clay, and the graves are dug, as you explained, into that yellow-grey clay, and then backfilled, as you explained a few moments ago, with the same yellow-grey clay. What happens then during the robbing process such that brown clay is then found, and what does that in turn tell you about process that -- that -- tell you about that next stage of the archaeological record and what happened after the graves were backfilled?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The presence of the mixed brown clay within the graves overlies the yellow-grey clay, it must have been deposited later, and it's consistent with the filling of the grave after removal of bodies and clay from those deposits of yellow-grey clay which are within the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: When the robbing of the grave is undertaken, how does that proceed? Are the bodies removed -- as revealed by the archaeological record, are the bodies removed one by one in a selected manner, or are they removed in another way with whatever equipment might be used?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The archaeological record, the evidence indicates bodies were truncated; that is, cut. Yellow-grey clay deposits are cut through. This is consistent with the use of heavy machinery to remove both clay and bodies from the grave, and there's nothing to indicate individual removal of bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: So the clay and bodies are resumed [sic] simultaneously with heavy equipment or heavy machinery and thus leaving a hole which may or may not be filled; is that right?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the archaeological record we uncovered is entirely consistent with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in this case, it was filled with the mixed brown clay that had previously been covering the site?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the mixed brown clay inside the grave was the same. It was consistent with the mixed brown clay which was covering that whole landscape. We could not discern differences in property between the mixed brown clay in the grave and that above and around the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Were you able to discern from how that mixed brown clay had been deposited into the previous grave-sites and over the rest of the grave area?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. Immediately to the north of the graves is large mound, which can be described as a hill of mine waste. This was formed of layers of mine waste in large blocks. The mixed brown clay layer started upon and spread from that hill of mine waste. The type of clay, and there are some very specific inclusions in the clay, we found across the whole site within the mixed brown clay layer are also found on the hill of mine waste. The mixed brown clay layer is, in fact, formed of several smaller thinner layers which are quite parallel. This is consistent with the moving of many, many tonnes of material using bulldozers to spread the material. So the findings are consistent with the mixed brown clay being pushed from the hill of mine waste across the whole area which acts as a covering.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And then in part filling the holes from which the bodies had been removed?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, exactly consistent with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And in addition to filling the holes, how much of the mixed brown clay from the hill of mine waste was eventually spread over the site to cover it up?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: We calculated about 40.000 cubic metres were removed during the excavation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And how deep was that at certain parts?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Nearest to the -- the hill of mine waste, 9 metres in depth, and further away it thinned out as it spread. At its furthest extent it was about a metre deep.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Before we leave this page, I just wanted to look at Figure 27 quickly. You say in the caption it's an image looking south-east showing excavator tool marks. These teeth impressions from the bucket of a large excavator are filled with mixed brown clay and are not weathered. Beyond the relatively obvious, it is showing the presence of the bucket of a large excavator. Does that also tell you anything about the length of time between the activity and the covering up of -- of the site with mixed brown clay?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the figure shows the teeth marks; that's the impressions made by the metal teeth on an excavator bucket. When they were excavated, they were found to be very sharp. By that I mean straight sides and edges. That's an indication that they were covered quite soon after they were made. If they'd been exposed for a length of time to the elements, to rain, I would not expect to see those sharp edges.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, we've just focused on the -- the archaeological record and what can be gleaned from it as -- through the prism of the dirt that was found or the clay that was found and where it was found. Can I now turn your attention to the bodies and body parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could go back to Figure 41 at page 46. If we could enlarge that slightly once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: With respect to the presence of either complete bodies or body parts, did you find a distinction between the areas within the robbing cuts and the areas of the main grave that were outside the robbing cuts?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Within the dash lines, that is, the areas described on the image as the robbing cuts, we have skeletonized body parts. Some bodies at the very bottom of the grave, but nearly all body parts. This contrasts with the other areas of the grave where we have intact piles of bodies within layers of yellow-grey clay where the bodies are complete. At the edges of those intact deposits, there are truncated bodies; that is, bodies missing parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Could we turn back a page to Figure 39.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And does that depict an example of the truncation that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you also find body parts outside the area of the main grave or the perimeter of the main grave?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, we did. Bodies and body parts were found in the mixed grey clay layers outside the grave to the west of the grave, and the points at which they were found can be seen in Figure 41.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Can -- can you describe the -- what this reveals, what these aspects of the archaeological record reveal about what happened? In short, can you tell us how this came to be: Body parts outside the -- and the disparity between the complete bodies in the undisturbed areas in yellow-grey clay and the body parts in the mixed brown clay in the disturbed areas?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, the truncation and trauma to bodies and removal of parts of those bodies, which are then found mixed with the clay and also found outside the grave, is consistent with removal and transport of bodies using heavy machinery.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And how is it that body parts end up outside the grave?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: This is consistent with bodies removed and then dropped when the mixed brown clay and -- mixed with the mixed brown clay, when that is then being bulldozed over the site.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And turning quickly to Figure 40 at page 46, is that an example of the truncation of body parts resulting from the process you describe?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it is. That's quite typical. It's a lower left leg with a foot in a sock and shoe with damage and breaking of the leg bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now, with respect to these dispersed body parts, was the investigation able to link various body parts found within the grave to body parts found outside the grave through DNA analysis?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. And similarly was it able to identify the links or associations between body parts found at Tomasica and body parts found elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And where else were parts of an individual person's body truncated and found at the Tomasica site also found?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: The Jakarina Kosa site from remains recovered in the 2001 excavation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Now going back to the conclusions section of your report, at paragraph 136, you then indicate that the whole area was then covered with a thick layer of mixed brown clay, et cetera. That's what you spoke about before, I take it, in connection with the presence and source of the mixed brown clay that came from the hill of mine waste?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And if we could turn quickly to Figure 32 at page 30, does that reflect the distinctive clay inclusions that you referred to that enabled you to identify the source of the mixed brown clay that covered the entirety of the site?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. On the right, you see some very distinct colours of clay. These were recovered from the hill of mine waste. The larger pieces on the left are taken from the mixed brown clay as examples across the site and may contain these distinct clay types, but "homogenized" is the word I use. It's mixed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you referring to Figure 23?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Figure 22, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Figure 22. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, I believe you mentioned earlier in connection with Figure 41 depicting the areas of disturbance in the undisturbed areas that within the areas of disturbance you found skeletonised body parts for the most part?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that in contrast to the preservation or relative preservation of the complete bodies found in the undisturbed areas?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And is that a further indication of the disturbance; i.e., the robbing of those areas within the dotted lines? And if so, explain quickly why that is.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: It is. Skeletonisation of remains occurs where they have contact with soil and oxygen. The dispersal of these body parts within the clay is an indicator that where the ground was disturbed, oxygen was then available in the soil for decomposition to occur and the contact of body parts with soil so hastens decomposition. The intact parts of bodies are compressed one on top of the other, and by being in a mass of bodies the compression prevents oxygen entering, which is why you have such a vivid contrast between the two areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: If we could turn to Figure 38 at page 44, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Did you say 48?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Figure 38 at page 44.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I wanted to look at that image in connection with paragraph 118 above it where you say bodies were for the most part clothed, some body parts and bones were not associated with clothing, some with fragmentary clothing. Hair, soft tissue, and skin survived in many bodies in the main grave piles. You indicate in the caption to the figure the image shows preservations of bodies within body deposit too in the main grave. They were compressed together preventing decomposition. You've already addressed the issue of compression and the effect of the clay on -- and -- and the relative timing of covering up in connection with the preservation of the bodies. I wanted to ask you a quick question about the clothing before we break, and that is: Did you identify the nature of the clothing, the personal effects found on the bodies as a result of this relative preservation; and is that addressed in paragraph 119, which is a long paragraph, at page 51? That is, the second paragraph on page 51.

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: Yes. The intact bodies were clothed. They had personal effects. There were documents with bodies, jewellery, money, everyday items normally carried on a person.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Was there anything unusual about the clothing?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: No. As observed during excavation, normal civilian attire seemed to be what bodies were wearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you find any military uniforms or other items associated with military activity during the excavation?

utterances.speaker: IAN HANSON
utterances.text: No military uniforms or other items associated with military activity were observed during this excavation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I see we're at the time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, you're coming closer to your two hours Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I realise that, and we will meet that deadline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then take a break first. We'd like to see you back there 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at ten minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Hanson, I just want to ask you briefly about two remaining related areas in your report, and those concern entomological or insect factors identified during the course of the excavation. The first is referred to at both paragraphs 103 and paragraphs 116. So first paragraph 103, page 35, you state there are no indicators as to how long the grave was open while it was being filled, although the preservation of the bodies and the lack of blowfly pupae cases suggest body piles were covered rapidly after being put in the grave.
